insights.claim: must-gather supports cross-Kubernetes distribution deployment (OpenShift, AKS, EKS, CKS) with an abstraction layer that replaces oc adm inspect with kubectl-based equivalents on non-OpenShift clusters.
insights.reasoning: The xks_util.sh file implements distribution detection via node metadata (kernel version, provider ID, OS image) and provides a complete kubectl-based alternative to oc adm inspect. This pattern enables the same must-gather image to be used across multiple cloud providers, which is architecturally significant for RHOAI's multi-cloud strategy.

insights.claim: must-gather executes component collection scripts in parallel when collecting all components, with per-job failure tracking that allows partial collection to succeed even when individual component gatherers fail.
insights.reasoning: The all-components collection path starts 14 gather scripts as background jobs, tracks their PIDs, and reports failures individually. This resilient-collection pattern means a missing or broken component does not prevent gathering data from other components, which is important for real-world diagnostic scenarios where the cluster may be partially degraded.

insights.claim: must-gather's resource collection list serves as an implicit inventory of all RHOAI platform components and their CRD API groups, making it a useful cross-reference for platform architecture completeness.

This list evolves with the platform and effectively documents the expected API surface of an RHOAI installation.
